opportunities.title: Repair the front door: a reachable, machine-readable and claimable web presence before any agent goes on top
opportunities.problem: The only ways a new customer can reach this 500k sq ft drayage and bonded-warehouse operator are a phone number that is invisible on phones and a ~70-field survey form. About/Services/Contact all point to '#', so there are no service pages for a buyer or an AI assistant to read; hours are stated three different ways; the Google listing carries an unclaimed profile; and the mobile menu still ships a template placeholder link (help@company.com) wrapped around the real e-mail address.
evidence: Top navigation items 'About us', 'Services' and 'Contact' all point to '#', so no about, service or contact page exists; robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return 404 - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=0 are set, and the stylesheet hides the address/e-mail/hours bar below 1023px and the header phone button below 1439px, so a phone visitor sees no phone number until the hamburger menu is opened - https://www.fedlogistics.com/css/responsive.css
The mobile menu's visible text info@fedlogistics.com is wrapped in a mailto:help@company.com link (template placeholder still live) - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

Hours conflict three ways: footer Mon-Fri 8:00am-4:30pm, mobile menu 8:00-6:00, Port Authority warehouse directory 0800-1700 - https://www.fedlogistics.com/ and https://aemdev.panynj.gov/content/dam/port/our-port/council-on-port-performance-pdf/available-warehouse-space.pdf

No JSON-LD/LocalBusiness schema, no meta description, page title is only the company name, and the sole H1 is a slogan ('Hundreds of customers trust our company') with no town, service or warehouse keyword - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

Earlier browser review (triage.json, batch b055) recorded a Google Maps listing rated 3.6 with 'Claim this business' shown, i.e. an unclaimed profile carrying the category, hours and site link; not re-verified in this pass - https://www.google.com/maps/search/Federation+Logistics+149+Black+Horse+Lane+North+Brunswick+NJ

The site's breadth of certifications (FDA, USDA, UIIA, US Customs bonded, SQF, ABC liquor licence) exists only as a logo block - a differentiator with no page to land on - https://www.fedlogistics.com/
opportunities.agent_design: Not an autonomous agent - a short build plus a light assistant. (1) Rebuild the front door: working nav, one page per service (warehousing, drayage, kitting, bonded, liquor-licensed, transportation), LocalBusiness/Service schema, a single canonical hours block, tap-to-call in the sticky header at all widths, remove the user-scalable=0 lock, and delete the placeholder mailto. (2) Claim and correct the Google Business Profile (services, hours, service area, photos) so Maps and voice assistants return the right answer. (3) Put a retrieval assistant on top that answers only from the new service pages and the verified hours/contact facts, with an escalation to the main line or the quote form after two turns. Human approves all public copy, hours and the listing edit before it goes live.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Off-the-shelf site builders do not produce per-service URLs, schema, canonical hours or a claimed listing, and a chatbot bolted onto today's site would be answering from page text that says the nav is broken and the hours contradict each other. The work is structural (information architecture, schema, listing ownership, mobile layout) plus a retrieval layer tied to approved copy - it needs someone who will also own the verification that Google and voice assistants now return the correct address, hours and services.

impact_estimate.range: No dollar figure is claimed. Measured in exposure: the business publishes a reachable path for only 42.5 hours per week (Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30), i.e. roughly 75% of the week has no published contact route; and on any screen narrower than 1439px - which is every phone and most tablets - the header phone button is hidden by CSS.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Office-hours coverage is computed from the footer hours the company publishes (42.5 of 168 hours = 25%). The 1439px breakpoint is read from the site's own responsive.css. The share of inbound interest that arrives outside those hours is unknown and not assumed here; a 2-week baseline of quote-form starts vs. submissions, calls and Maps views would convert this into a number before any revenue claim is made. The Google rating (3.6) and unclaimed status come from the earlier browser review (triage.json) and are treated as unverified.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: working navigation and 5-6 service pages with schema and a single source of truth for hours and contact; tap-to-call verified at 390px and 768px; placeholder assets removed; Google Business Profile claimed and corrected; a read-only retrieval assistant answering from those pages with an escalation path; before/after baseline of form starts, form submissions, calls and Maps views so the next phase has a number to beat.

opportunities.title: Quote-intake agent that turns the 70-field 'Customer Survey' into a structured rate request with an acknowledgement and a follow-up loop
opportunities.problem: Every inbound lead has to complete a ~70-input survey - 12 monthly volume percentages, pallet grade mix, SKU counts, batch/lot sensitivity, EDI/fax/e-mail order mix - before a human speaks to them, and the result posts to quote.php with no acknowledgement, no CRM record and no scheduler. Staff then read and re-key that free text into whatever holds the rate build, from an office open Mon-Fri 8:00-4:30.
evidence: Quote intake is one long form headlined 'Customer Survey' covering inbound, storage, outbound and communication sections with 12 monthly volume fields, pallet specs, batch/lot sensitivity and EDI percentages, submitted by a single 'Send message' button that posts back to quote.php - https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php

No CRM, chat widget, booking widget, quote calculator, tracking portal or customer login exists on either live page; the only interactive elements are the quote form and a Google Maps embed - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

The form itself records that verbal orders are not accepted at the warehouse and that order channels are a mix of EDI/electronic, fax, e-mail or other - i.e. exception handling is concentrated on a small back-office group - https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php
The site names no WMS, TMS, EDI translator or inventory-visibility tool; carrier integrations appear only as UPS and FedEx logos - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

The company claims 4 NJ locations and 500k+ sq ft including a 104,451 sq ft South Brunswick lease signed in Nov 2024, while the public front door still describes one North Brunswick address and one phone line - https://www.fedlogistics.com/ and https://rebusinessonline.com/federation-distribution-services-signs-104451-sf-industrial-lease-in-south-brunswick-new-jersey/

Form validation bans single quotes in free-text fields (an SQL-escape workaround) and posts to a hand-built PHP handler, consistent with no form platform in place - https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php
opportunities.agent_design: An intake agent sits in front of the form. Trigger: a new submission to quote.php, an inbound e-mail to info@, or a missed call logged by the office. The agent (1) acknowledges immediately with a reference number and a realistic response window; (2) reads the free text and normalizes it into a fixed schema - volume by month, pallet count and type, SKU count, temperature/food-grade needs, bonded or ABC requirement, inbound mode, outbound mode, EDI mix; (3) asks only for what is missing, one question at a time, by e-mail or SMS reply, instead of blocking the prospect at field 40; (4) flags bonded/ABC/food-grade requests for the compliance owner and drafts the internal rate-build sheet; (5) chases silence on a 2/5/10-day cadence and writes every touch to a CRM record. Human approves every rate sent and every qualification judgement; the agent never quotes a price, commits space or accepts a booking. Systems touched: quote.php (or its replacement), mailbox, CRM, calendar. Runs on the brokerage-style exception queue first, then the order-intake side once the rate path is trusted.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot acknowledge asynchronously, keep a per-prospect state machine across e-mail and web, normalize messy 70-field free text into a rate-build schema, or write to a CRM; and it cannot be trusted with volume bands and bonded-status data. This needs event triggers on two channels, a schema and validation layer, escalation rules, and an audit log of what was told to which prospect - and it touches customer-owned commercial data (volumes, SKUs, trading-partner mixes) that the industry brief flags as needing private or VPC deployment.

impact_estimate.range: Conservatively ~$7,000-$23,000 per year of clerk/planner hours recovered (roughly 6-15 hours per week), before counting leads that today abandon the survey unfinished.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Basis: NJ median wage for Shipping, Receiving and Inventory Clerks is $45,440/yr ($21.85/hr) and for Production, Planning and Expediting Clerks is $62,710/yr ($30.15/hr), over ~50 worked weeks. The 6-15 hr/week band is an INFERENCE, not a measured figure: it assumes 8-25 quote requests or order exceptions per week at 10-25 minutes of read-and-re-key plus follow-up each, and that the agent removes 60-80% of that handling while a human still reviews every rate. No measured 3PL study of agent time savings exists (industry brief data gap), so no throughput or win-rate uplift is claimed; the form-abandonment share is unmeasured and deliberately excluded.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: one schema, an acknowledgement and reference-number flow on every quote.php submission, the gap-filling question loop over e-mail, an internal rate-build sheet generated from each request, a CRM record per prospect with a 3-touch follow-up cadence, and a weekly report of submissions, completion, response time and follow-up outcome. Human approval gate on all outbound rate content.

opportunities.title: Bonded, ABC and food-grade document agent: a compliance knowledge base plus a document-request portal for clients and staff
opportunities.problem: The firm advertises US Customs bonded, ABC liquor-licensed, SQF, FDA and USDA scopes across four sites, but offers no portal, upload, appointment or document-request flow - the only document-adjacent channel is the info@ mailbox - so compliance paperwork and 'what do you need from me' questions are routed through one shared inbox and one person's memory, against deadlines that are machine-checkable and unforgiving.
evidence: Certifications block claims FDA, USDA, UIIA, US Customs bonded, SQF and ABC liquor-licensed storage - https://www.fedlogistics.com/
No careers page, no supplier/vendor page and no document upload for customs or ABC paperwork; the only document-adjacent channel is the info@ mailbox - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

Port Authority warehouse directory describes the North Brunswick site as food-grade handling food products (Oct 2023 edition) - https://aemdev.panynj.gov/content/dam/port/our-port/council-on-port-performance-pdf/available-warehouse-space.pdf
Bonded and liquor-licensed storage across 4 claimed NJ sites, with drayage of 55k containers a year from the NJ ports to those facilities (company marketing figures) - https://www.fedlogistics.com/

Industry constraint: cargo release documents must be filed within 15 calendar days of arrival and the entry summary (CBP Form 7501) plus estimated duty deposit within 10 working days of release - https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/entry-summary

O*NET lists compliance software for customs/trade filing (Kewill Compliance Partner) as a tool of the shipping/receiving clerk role, which is exactly the work being handled by hand here - https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-5071.00
opportunities.agent_design: A retrieval agent over the company's own documents plus a thin client-facing portal. Ingestion: customs bond and importer-of-record packet templates, ABC/liquor licence conditions, SQF and FDA/USDA procedures, per-client routing guides and SOPs, dock-appointment rules per site. Triggers: (1) a client question by e-mail or portal message; (2) a status change on a document request; (3) a deadline clock - arrival date plus 15 calendar days, release plus 10 working days, licence expiry, bond renewal. The agent answers with citations to the exact SOP clause, drafts the missing-document request to the client, assembles a checklist per shipment or per licence renewal, and escalates any answer it cannot ground. A human compliance owner approves every filing instruction and every answer that touches a regulator. Deadlines are deterministic code with an audit trail, not model judgement. Portal work is deliberately small: a tokenized upload link and a status page, not a WMS replacement.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A general chatbot cannot be allowed near customs-bond and ABC licence language: answers must cite the firm's own SOPs, deadlines must be computed in code with an audit trail, client documents must be stored per-client with access control, and expiry/bond clocks must fire without anyone remembering. It also requires ingesting and version-controlling the firm's own paperwork - which is the actual deliverable, not the chat interface. Document and inventory data are commercially confidential, so this runs in a private/VPC deployment per the brief's constraint.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $2,500-$11,000 per year of clerk and customer-service hours on document chasing and status answering (2-8 hours per week), with the larger value being avoided rework on hard customs deadlines that is not priced here.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Basis: NJ medians of $21.85/hr for shipping/receiving/inventory clerks ($45,440/yr) and $22.95/hr for customer service representatives ($47,740/yr), over ~50 weeks. The 2-8 hr/week band is an INFERENCE: it assumes 3-10 document requests or status questions a week at 15-20 minutes of lookup, drafting and chasing each, and that 60-80% becomes agent-assisted with human sign-off. Nothing is claimed for detention, demurrage or penalty exposure because no Federation-specific volume of late filings was observed. The site's 55k-container figure is company marketing and unverified, so it is used only to describe scale, not to compute hours.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 4 weeks on one scope (customs-bonded imports, or ABC licence renewals): ingest that scope's SOPs and licence conditions, build the citation-backed Q&A, wire the deterministic deadline clocks with alerts, stand up a tokenized document-upload page for 3-5 friendly clients, and deliver a weekly exception report of missing documents and imminent deadlines. Human compliance owner signs off every outbound instruction.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (23/30): the front-door and quote-intake problems are unusually well documented for a small firm - two independent passes (profile plus triage.json batch b055) found dead navigation, a phone number hidden by CSS below 1439px, a live template placeholder mailto, three conflicting sets of hours, no schema or meta description, an unclaimed Google listing, and a ~70-field 'Customer Survey' as the sole online quote path with no acknowledgement or CRM behind it. The weakest pain is the third opportunity, which rests on the company's own bonded/ABC/FDA/USDA/SQF claims plus the absence of any upload or portal - the document-chasing pain itself is an inference, not an observed complaint. Fit (17/20): G, A and C are direct matches to the stated capability set, and the front door genuinely comes first - an agent layered on dead links and contradictory hours would just automate a wrong answer. Ability to pay (12/20): a real operation (500k+ sq ft claimed, 15 power units and 16 drivers under USDOT 935795, a 104,451 sq ft lease signed in Nov 2024, ~$1.1k average weekly wage county benchmark context) but family-run, with an externally credited developer, no in-house marketing or IT function, and no spending signal such as job postings for ops-tech roles. Ease (12/15): the site is static PHP, the org is small, the named principal (Les Sokoloff, President) can decide, and a front-door pilot needs no legacy integration - the rate is off partly because the quote agent's real target system (the WMS/TMS holding the rate build) is unnamed and will need discovery. Strategic (13/15): the pattern - NJ 3PL/drayage operator with bonded and food-grade scope, a neglected template site and a survey-as-quote-form - repeats across Middlesex County's 251 NAICS-493 establishments and 27,047 warehousing employees, so the build is resellable with only content changes. Physical/edge (E) was considered and deliberately not among the top 3: no avenues.json was supplied for this task, so no verified design, hardware or legal note was available, and the only floor-side signal in the profile is the company's own marketing counter (55k containers, 100k pallets a year) with no evidence of a yard, quality or temperature pain - a camera or sensor pilot here would rest on stacked inferences (handled in walk_in_checks: if the founder visits, ask about yard/container counting and temperature logging at the food-grade and bonded areas, and note that any CCTV, access-control or security use requires a licensed NJ alarm or electrical contractor under N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2).

best_evidence_signal: The only online quote path is a ~70-field form headlined 'Customer Survey' posting to quote.php, while the live mobile menu still wraps the real e-mail address in a mailto:help@company.com template placeholder - https://www.fedlogistics.com/quote.php and https://www.fedlogistics.com/
